la-gloria-cubana-dr--la-gloria-cubana-cl.description: The blend that started La Gloria Cubana, first made by Ernesto Perez-Carrillo and now rolled at the El Credito factory in the Dominican Republic. An aged Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper covers a Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. A medium smoke of chocolate and leather with earth, molasses-like sweetness, a touch of citrus and a cedar finish.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Classic
Holt's – La Gloria Cubana

la-gloria-cubana-dr--la-gloria-cubana-ma.description: The Classic La Gloria Cubana blend under a deep brown Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper, with the same Nicaraguan binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. The dark leaf adds weight and sweetness: expect a smooth, medium smoke of dark chocolate, leather, wood and pepper, finishing on cedar.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Classic Maduro
Holt's – La Gloria Cubana

la-gloria-cubana-dr--serie-r.description: Serie R became known in the 1990s for its thick ring gauges. A Dominican and Nicaraguan filler sits in a Nicaraguan binder, under an aged Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper or, for the maduro, Connecticut Broadleaf. It smokes medium to full with coffee, chocolate and a marked spiciness; the maduro adds earth, wood and baking spice.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Serie R
La Gloria Cubana – Serie R Maduro
Holt's – La Gloria Cubana Serie R

la-gloria-cubana-dr--serie-r-esteli.description: A Nicaraguan puro made in Estelí, blended from ligero and viso leaves from several farms under a thick, oily Jalapa sun-grown wrapper. It comes only in large ring gauges. Medium to full, it shows spice and coffee with a nutty, floral side and a touch of leather.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Serie R Esteli
Holt's – Serie R Estelí
Cigar Coop – La Gloria Cubana Serie R Esteli review

thirds.notes: Cocoa and natural tobacco, with red pepper close behind and strongest on the retrohale.
Natural tobacco and its sweetness take the lead; cocoa drops back and pepper returns.
Tobacco and pepper in front, with cocoa giving way to an earthy note; no harshness.

la-gloria-cubana-dr--serie-r-esteli-madu.description: Rolled in Estelí with the same Nicaraguan binder and filler as Serie R Estelí, but under an oily Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. Strong and sweet at once, it brings earth, dark cocoa and espresso bean with nutty notes, spice and a smoky, leathery aroma.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Serie R Esteli Maduro
Holt's – Serie R Estelí Maduro

la-gloria-cubana-dr--serie-r-black.description: A Nicaraguan puro built on Jalapa tobacco from an independent grower, fermented for a full year and aged for two and a half more. A Jalapa ligero wrapper and Jalapa binder hold Jalapa and Estelí filler. The maker describes a rich, medium to full smoke with spice, coffee and a nutty, floral character.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Serie R Black

la-gloria-cubana-dr--serie-r-black-madur.description: The maduro version of Serie R Black: aged Nicaraguan long filler in a Nicaraguan binder, under a Connecticut Broadleaf wrapper. It keeps the balance of the original with more depth, bringing pepper, earth and coffee together with a slightly sweet, creamy note from the dark leaf.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Serie R Black Maduro
Casas Fumando – La Gloria Cubana Serie R Black Maduro review

thirds.notes: Sweetness first, then a sour, woody edge, dirty earth and a heavy pepper that sharpens through the nose.
Earth moves forward and covers most of the sweetness; the sour note now reads as lemon zest.
Earth keeps building, sweetness returns and becomes cocoa-like in the last inches, with manageable spice.

la-gloria-cubana-dr--serie-s.description: Serie S was the first La Gloria Cubana with a Mexican San Andrés wrapper, grown in the volcanic soil of Veracruz, over an Estelí binder and Dominican and Nicaraguan filler. It keeps the brand's large ring gauges. A medium to full smoke with gentle sweetness, a subtle earthiness and light spice; a maduro version adds leathery depth.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Serie S
La Gloria Cubana – Serie S Maduro
Cigar Coop – La Gloria Cubana Serie S Robusto Gordo review

thirds.notes: Coffee and earth lead, with cocoa, baking spice, mixed pepper and a faint sour-candy note.
Coffee and earth take turns in front as pepper rises and the cocoa largely fades.
Pepper joins coffee and earth up front, with baking spice behind.

la-gloria-cubana-dr--esteli.description: La Gloria Cubana Estelí is a bolder, modern take on the Classic. A wrapper from Nicaragua's Jalapa Valley covers a Honduran Jamastran binder and Honduran Jamastran and La Entrada filler. It is a spicy smoke, medium to full in body, with cedar, baking spice and white pepper.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Esteli
Blind Man's Puff – La Gloria Cubana Estelí Robusto blind review

thirds.notes: Nuts and leather with oak woodiness, over a grassy, hay-like background and a slightly salty finish.
Coffee grows stronger and sweetness with baking spice appears around the midpoint.
Nuts, leather and wood with baking spice and a dark-roast coffee edge, as strength and body step up.

la-gloria-cubana-dr--medio-tiempo.description: Named for the medio tiempo leaves that sometimes grow above the top priming of a sun-grown Connecticut Havana plant, visible as a dark band at the foot. Filler from Connecticut, the Dominican Republic, Nicaragua and Honduras sits in a U.S. Broadleaf binder under an Ecuadorian Sumatra wrapper. Expect leather, coffee, nuts and a buttery texture with light spice.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Medio Tiempo

la-gloria-cubana-dr--intencion.description: Intención returns to the brand's roots with bold blends and large ring gauges. A Mexican San Andrés wrapper and Indonesian binder hold a four-country filler of Estelí ligero and viso and Honduran Jamastran viso and La Entrada ligero. The maker describes a balance of chocolate, leather and spice.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Intención
Tiny Tim's Blog – La Gloria Cubana Intención Gran Robusto review

thirds.notes: Apricot and brown sugar over earth, tanned leather and black coffee, with a lingering black pepper.
The sweetness is gone; black coffee and earth rise sharply with leather and dark chocolate.
Black coffee and earth with an unexpected pecan note as the body turns full.

la-gloria-cubana-dr--los-gloriosos.description: Los Gloriosos brings La Gloria Cubana back to its founder: it is made at Casa Carrillo in collaboration with Ernesto Perez-Carrillo. An Ecuadorian Habano wrapper covers a Nicaraguan binder and filler from Jalapa, Condega and the Dominican Republic. An earthy, balanced smoke of leather, espresso, spice and cocoa.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Los Gloriosos
Cigar Coop – La Gloria Cubana Los Gloriosos Toro review

thirds.notes: Natural tobacco and wood blend in front, with cedar, earth and white then black pepper behind.
A musty note comes forward as the tobacco and wood recede; pepper builds slowly.
Wood and must lead with more pepper, and the finish turns somewhat harsh.

la-gloria-cubana-dr--spanish-press.description: Spanish Press revives a pre-embargo Cuban practice: the cigars are pressed in wooden boxes to remove air pockets and set their square shape. A Nicaraguan Jalapa wrapper and San Andrés binder hold Nicaraguan, Dominican Piloto Cubano and Olor, and Brazilian Mata Fina filler. A medium-bodied smoke of nuts, earth, toast and light sweetness.

sources.title: La Gloria Cubana – Spanish Press
Cigar Coop – La Gloria Cubana Spanish Press Robusto review

thirds.notes: Natural tobacco and red licorice lead over earth and mixed pepper, with baking spice joining later.
Natural tobacco becomes the sole lead as the licorice fades and the pepper turns to black pepper and grows.
Tobacco still leads with steady black pepper and touches of licorice, earth and baking spice.
